sentences.text:
(PER : HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE MAULIK J.SHELAT)
1. Heard learned advocate Ms.Kirti S. Pathak, appearing for the appellant and Mr.Mayur V. Dhotare for Nanavati Associates.

2. The present appeals are filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act (herein after referred to as 'the MV Act') challenging common judgment and award dated 29.10.2012 passed by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (Aux.), 4 th Additional Sessions Court, Bharuch in Motor Accident Claim Petition Nos.792 and 793 of 2007.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (Aux.), 4 th Additional Sessions Court, Bharuch
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petition Nos.792 and 793 of 2007
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/715/2013 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 3.

The principal contention raised in the present appeal is that at the time of accident, the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence then Insurance Company was wrongly held liable to pay compensation by Tribunal.
4. The driving licence of Opponent No.1 - driver of tempo was a licence to drive a transport vehicle of LMV category.
The vehicle involved in the accident insured with the appellant and so tempo bearing registration no. GJ.16.X.1775 falls under the category of LMV.
These are undisputed facts on record.

5. The issue is now squarely covered by Full Bench Decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Mukul Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in 2017 (14) SSC 663 and recently by constitution bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company vs. Rambha Devi & ors reported in 2014 SCC Supreme Court online 3183.
6.

entities.text: Mukul Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in 2017 (14) SSC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Company vs. Rambha Devi & ors reported in 2014 SCC Supreme Court online 3183
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in view of the aforesaid facts and position of law, the appeals are meritless and require to be dismissed and hence, both the appeals are DISMISSED.

7. The amount, which is lying before the Tribunal or in the FDR shall be disbursed in favour of the claimants on proper verification through RTGS/NEFT or any other banking mode in accordance with law by the Tribunal.
In view of the dismissal of both these appeals, we are not inclined to examine the merits of the application.

Nonetheless, it is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/715/2013 ORDER DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined open for the original claimants to pursue legal remedy available in law to claim the amount, which according to the claimants, is short fall, if any, deposited by the insurance company.
In view of the above, the Civil Applications are also disposed of accordingly.
